chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Barqi, from Asram ibn Hawshab, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
"The wadis (valleys/streambeds) of the Sanctuary (Haram) flow in the Plain (Hill), and the wadis of the Plain do not flow in the Sanctuary."

key_terms.أَوْدِيَةُ: Wadis (valleys or streambeds where water flows)
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (the sacred precincts of Mecca)
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The Plain (the area outside the sacred precincts)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the wadis of the Haram and the Hill regarding the flow of water for pilgrims?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) employs a natural hydrological metaphor to explain the legal principle of *khuruj al-haram* (exit from the sacred precinct) regarding the minor pilgrimage (Umrah). It clarifies that while the sanctity and restrictions of the Haram extend outward into the Hill, the reverse is not true, establishing a clear boundary for pilgrims transitioning between the two zones. This ruling is crucial for determining when a pilgrim is fully released from Ihram restrictions after completing the Tawaf and Sa'i.
